question: Express the matrix $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\4&0&5\\-2&1&6\end{bmatrix}$$ as the sum of a symmetric matrix and a skew-symmetric matrix by using its transpose, and verify directly that the matrices obtained possess the required symmetry properties and add to $A$.
explanation:
Applying the Required Form

For any square matrix $A$, we may write $$A=\frac{1}{2}(A+A')+\frac{1}{2}(A-A')$$ Here, $$A'=\begin{bmatrix}2&4&-2\\-1&0&1\\3&5&6\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $$A+A'=\begin{bmatrix}4&3&1\\3&0&6\\1&6&12\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$A-A'=\begin{bmatrix}0&-5&5\\5&0&4\\-5&-4&0\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, let $$S=\frac{1}{2}(A+A')=\begin{bmatrix}2&\frac{3}{2}&\frac{1}{2}\\\frac{3}{2}&0&3\\\frac{1}{2}&3&6\end{bmatrix}$$ and $$K=\frac{1}{2}(A-A')=\begin{bmatrix}0&-\frac{5}{2}&\frac{5}{2}\\\frac{5}{2}&0&2\\-\frac{5}{2}&-2&0\end{bmatrix}$$

Verification

Transposing $S$ gives $$S'=\begin{bmatrix}2&\frac{3}{2}&\frac{1}{2}\\\frac{3}{2}&0&3\\\frac{1}{2}&3&6\end{bmatrix}=S$$ so $S$ is symmetric. Also, $$K'=\begin{bmatrix}0&\frac{5}{2}&-\frac{5}{2}\\-\frac{5}{2}&0&-2\\\frac{5}{2}&2&0\end{bmatrix}=-K$$ so $K$ is skew-symmetric. Finally, $$S+K=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1&3\\4&0&5\\-2&1&6\end{bmatrix}=A$$ Thus, the given matrix has been expressed as the sum of a symmetric matrix and a skew-symmetric matrix.
